result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another, from other species, and from the Earth itself.

This shift would dissolve the roots of greed, exploitation, and conflict, because harming another (or the planet) would be as unthinkable as harming oneself. Empathy would become the default, not the exception. Systems built on extraction—economic, social, environmental—would collapse under the weight of their own absurdity, replaced by structures that nourish collective well-being.

It wouldn’t erase difference or conflict, but it would recast them: disagreements would arise from a place of shared stakes, not zero-sum competition. The question wouldn’t be *"What can I take?"* but *"What can we grow?"*

(And yes, I’m aware this sounds utopian. But the alternative—perpetuating the myth that we’re isolated atoms bumping against each other—has led us to the brink. Why not aim for the impossible?)
